findings.title: Use stored enablement rather than organization-aware enablement for invalidation
findings.body: The original model passed to this method comes from getById(), which wraps isEnabled() to return false when the associated organization is disabled. The updated model can also fail the login predicate because the update sets hideOnLogin or linkOnly. Consequently, both predicates can be false and this branch skips invalidation even though the IDP is still present in an existing login cache. For example, populate the cache for a public organization IDP, disable the organization, hide the IDP, and re-enable the organization. The cached ID remains, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), so the hidden IDP is displayed again. Compare the persisted IDP flags independently of organization enablement when deciding whether query membership changed.

findings.title: Do not republish an old query under a fresh revision
findings.body: When adding an uncached organization search, this code copies all searches from the previously read query but publishes them using a revision obtained after invalidateObject() and the current counter. If another transaction changes login eligibility and invalidates this key between reading the old query and invalidateObject(), the old searches are copied back under the newer revision. For example, enabling an IDP can invalidate a cached empty organization result, only for a concurrent search for another organization to restore that empty result. Subsequent logins then omit the newly enabled provider until another invalidation or eviction. The merged query must retain or validate the revision of the original query rather than treating its old results as freshly loaded.

findings.title: Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases
findings.body: The test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback removes the literal alias "alias" instead. The same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. Cleanup therefore requests removal of nonexistent providers, which can fail with a not-found response, and leaves the created providers behind if the realm is reused. Capture each actual alias when registering its cleanup callback.
